quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, where should you position your motorcycle in your lane?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The center of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
Either the right or center portions of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This position gives you the best view of the lane ahead.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions frequently to prevent boredom.
Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around your motorcycle.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions are always changing. Choose the lane position that gives you the most space around your motorcycle and makes you easiest for other drivers to see.

questions.question: Do approved helmets limit your ability to see?

options.text: Yes, they can limit your side vision.
No, approved helmets allow you to see everything you need.
Yes, helmets are dangerous to wear.
You do not have to wear one if you think it limits your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, approved helmets allow you to see everything you need.
questions.explanation: Approved helmets do not limit your vision. You can see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop your motorcycle quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: For the quickest stop, apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What protection do goggles provide?

options.text: Protection for your eyes only.
The same protection as a face shield.
The same protection as a windshield.
Protection for your entire face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protection for your eyes only.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only, not your face. A face shield gives better protection for your whole face. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: Which action helps reduce your chance of a crash?

options.text: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
Follow other drivers too closely.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Do not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible, signal your intentions, keep space around your motorcycle, look ahead at least 12 seconds, identify hazards, and be ready for changing conditions.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good quality of motorcycle riding clothing?

options.text: It protects you in a crash.
It protects you from heat and cold.
It protects you from hot and moving motorcycle parts.
It is uncomfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is uncomfortable.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothing should protect you in a crash, shield you from heat and cold, protect you from road debris and motorcycle parts, and keep you comfortable.

questions.question: What happens when your rear tire skids?

options.text: It is not dangerous.
You lose the ability to steer.
It will fix itself automatically.
It is only dangerous if the front tire also skids.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose the ability to steer.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is very dangerous and can cause a serious crash. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel. When the wheel locks, you cannot steer. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front.
Do not signal so you do not distract the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing. Signal your intentions, check for traffic, and pass only when safe. Signal again and return to your lane when it is safe.

questions.question: Why might you move into another lane while turning?

options.text: You are taking the turn too fast.
The lane is too narrow.
You do not know how to steer.
The lane is too wide.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are taking the turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: You operate the rear brake of a motorcycle with your right foot.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use the rear brake only.
Use the front brake only.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes together at the same time.

questions.question: What should you do if the front wheel locks?

options.text: Keep holding the brake until the skid stops.
Release the front brake and do not use it again.
Release the front brake, then squeeze it quickly.
Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, let go of the brake completely right away. Then apply the brake again with smooth pressure.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, which of the following is NOT a hazard?

options.text: Extended mirrors.
Objects thrown from other vehicles.
Wind blasts.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the vehicle's mirrors, wind gusts, and objects that may be thrown. Headlights are not a hazard when another vehicle passes you.

questions.question: How should you help drivers merge from an entrance ramp into your lane?

options.text: Stay in your lane.
Move to another lane if you can.
Do not worry about it since they are merging.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if you can.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging onto the highway may not see your motorcycle. Give them space by changing lanes if possible.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, which brake should you use?

options.text: Use the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Use the brake on the tire that is flat.
Use both brakes.
Do not use either brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the tire that is still good.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When passing another vehicle.
When you will slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is smaller than a car's. Flashing it helps other drivers see you, especially when you slow down faster than expected.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Distances are easier to judge at night than during the day.
Using high beam headlights always makes it hard to see.
Use only one lane position.
Reduce your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: At night, slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles. Use your high beam when there is no other traffic. Be ready to change your lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black lettering or symbols are warning signs. They alert drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: The body eliminates one drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?

options.text: One drink
Two drinks
Three drinks
Four drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining.

questions.question: How should the front brake be used?

options.text: It is too dangerous for inexperienced riders.
It works best when used alone.
It should sometimes help the rear brake.
It should be used together with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be used together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What are the penalties for drinking and riding?

options.text: Severe.
Left to a judge's decision.
Not very harsh.
Not required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Severe.
questions.explanation: Oregon law has strict mandatory penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous to ride a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: If one rider in a group wants to go faster than the others, what should the group do?

options.text: Let that rider go ahead and meet up at a planned location later.
Speed up to keep pace with that rider.
Split up so each rider can go their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let that rider go ahead and meet up at a planned location later.
questions.explanation: If one member of a group wants to ride faster, let them go ahead and plan to meet at a specific location later.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a motorcycle horn?

options.text: It has no real use.
Other drivers usually cannot hear it.
It can quickly get someone's attention.
It should never be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can quickly get someone's attention.
questions.explanation: Your horn can help you get someone's attention quickly. However, a motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn, so other drivers may not hear it. Never rely only on your horn to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?

options.text: After starting the motorcycle
Before starting the motorcycle
While riding
At a traffic signal

questions.correctAnswerText: Before starting the motorcycle
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before you start your motorcycle. Adjust them so you can see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you.
